item.title: Occupy Dallas
item.dc:creator: Blimpy
item.description: This revolution will not be televised…because it’s not a revolution. Don’t get me wrong, I’m sympathetic to the cause. item.content:encoded:
This revolution will not be televised…because it’s not a revolution.

Don’t get me wrong, I’m sympathetic to the cause.  Wealth disparity in this country is massive (as bad as it’s been since 1928), real income has declined substantially in the last decade, special interest corporate money does buy politicians…but I violated my cardinal rule by researching a place too long before I went there via the Occupy Dallas facebook page.  Two days ago 24 members were arrested for linking arms in front of a bank downtown and stopping normal people from entering while ragging on them to close their accounts.  Umm, that’s a crime, it’s called disturbing the peace, harassment, what have you.  What if all the Texas Republicans who disagree with #Occupy linked arms and prevented the tent city members from getting back to their shanty town by City Hall?

Say what you will, but I've never been arrested for no reason

So on their facebook was a “desperate plea” for information regarding the harassment of these prisoners and them not being given access to water, i.e. a “desperate plea” for attention.  Well, around the 5th comment was someone saying “all the prisoners with a fixed address and no criminal record have already been released, and they only had bottled water withheld, there’s a fountain in every cell.”  Yikes, that was actually the truth, rail against the news media all you want, but a half-truth is just that.  We’re talking about jail here for breaking a legitimate law, 30 years ago you would have got the phone book treatment in a heartbeat, and if I’m in there for stabbing a guy over a vial of crack, damn right I’m going to be harassing you.

Oh, and on the occupydallas.org site under the Donations section they are asking for a larger coffee maker.  To the next person I hear comparing #Occupy crackdowns with Tahir Square, I would be happy to go Mubarek on them, which would entail the internet being shut down and them dying.  We get to vote, we get lawyers in jail.  And yeah, I heard about Oakland, but that place is a different animal, there was a larger riot when I was there last year and you’ll notice all the news articles describe the protestors as “for the most part peaceful”.  Well, one bad apple I’m afraid folks.  The main thing it proves to me is the #Occupy movement’s best chance comes through the authorities acting foolishly, not them acting wisely.

I'm at least behind that

Arriving at the Dallas site the next morning, my honest initial reaction was “this is sad”.  Walking up I had a good angle with the tents in the background and a half dozen cops just standing and chatting (who I learned were in fact there to deal with the numerous nightly reports of the protestors robbing each other…ironic, I know.)  As I was snapping the shot I heard one protester asking another where she was scuttling off to, having not noticed them standing to my left in the slightest, to which she cast a fierce glance in my direction and said “this guy’s trying to take my picture.”  If you’d been involved in the movement the several weeks it’s been happening, surely countless other photographers and news media who don’t have footlong hair and haven’t bathed in a week have spotted you to put on their US government/Google conspiracy hit list.  And shouldn’t you be trying to get me to put a positive spin on this rather than being hostile and ashamed?  Oh, and last but not least, you weren’t even in the shot, bitch.

During my hour hanging around camp I had 2 protesters ask me for spare change to buy a Dr. Pepper (it was invented here, there’s a local version made with pure cane sugar, it’s a fair request) and 3 normal civilians ask me why there were tents everywhere.  I told one it was an offshoot of Occupy Wall Street to which she replied “what’s that?” so it’s equally sad on both sides.  While I was dropping off a jug of water and a spare tarp I brought, I asked a fellow if they had any actions planned today, and he told me “oh, we’ll march somewhere.”  Exactly.

10% of the 99% think this is a joke

The one saving grace of the whole affair was a legit homeless black guy named Jay who I spoke with for a good 10 minutes.  He had things to say about unemployment in Spain and the globalized economy being intertwined, that the US dollar was nothing but a promissory note, that he’d had several jobs where his employer would only ever give him 24 hours a week, whatever the magic number is to not have to give benefits.  That was a great conversation.  Oh, and there were some good signs posted around the camp.  And yes, the system is broken and this raising awareness can’t hurt, but there’s something eerily off about what’s happening there considering I had every intention of staying at least one night and almost immediately abandoned such a notion.  Taking a look at their poster Occupations of our Occupiers, people had written down “Philosopher, Revolutionary, Leader, Creative Person, Graffiti Student and Pimp”.  None of those are occupations and are case in point why movements like We Are The 53% (who pay income tax and don’t sympathize) have sprung up.

Feeling that I needed to cleanse myself by buying some Starbucks and throwing out half of it just because I can, I headed towards the JFK Plaza.  Oswald was a pretty good shot!  And so was J. Edgar Hoover dressed in drag as the second shooter on the grassy knoll, or however the guy selling leaflets on the corner tells it.  But on my return pass by the Occupy camp to where I parked, sure enough there was a shirtless guy with a shaved head but for a single dreadlock down to his waist playing hula hoop in the middle of the street quite obviously high as the goddam sky and the cops laughing their asses off in the background.  And I walked right past laughing with them.

Here’s the gallery.

item.title: BlimpyB, World Series good luck charm
item.dc:creator: Blimpy
item.description: I would say I’m “just outside Dallas”, but the place is so sprawling and huge you could say that for 100+ miles in any direction. So many shopping malls…the Starbucks are bigger than any I’ve ever seen. In the midst of it all, Ft. Worth is actually remarkably cool, it’s got a ton of Western [...]
item.content:encoded:
I would say I’m “just outside Dallas”, but the place is so sprawling and huge you could say that for 100+ miles in any direction.  So many shopping malls…the Starbucks are bigger than any I’ve ever seen.  In the midst of it all, Ft. Worth is actually remarkably cool, it’s got a ton of Western character and obviously a lot more money than Amarillo, Lubbock or Abilene, while still remaining just as Bible Belt.   Not really planning on spending much time in Dallas, JFK skull fragments and conspiracy theories aren’t really my thing.

Speaking of the Bible Belt, interestingly enough freedom trumps all here and the Texan attitude is truly one to be applauded.  You could sit right down next to a cowboy hat wearing, truck driving fella at the bar and tell him “I support Obama, don’t believe in God and come from a country where men can marry other men” and he’d probably look at you sideways for a second then say “I ain’t in agreement with none of that, but if it works for y’all that’s just fine and dandy.”  Imagine the reaction you’d get in Vancouver, Portland or San Francisco saying “I’m a card carrying Republican, I believe being homosexual is a sin against the word of almighty Jesus and people who get caught with a half gram of marijuana should go to federal prison.”  See where I’m going with that?  Beers, steers and queers baby, fuck it, who cares.

Oh right, that World Series reference in the title.  So the Rangers are in it, just as they were last year battling San Francisco while I was there.  It’s kind of creeping me out a lot that’s only 1700 miles as the crow flies, and I mean yeah, I drove all the way down the Cali coast not to mention took 4 months off, but woah, that’s still 7 miles a day while I’ve been in Bessie, this walking Quebecois freak who ditched his wife and kids moves faster than me.  Perhaps that I’m currently planning 1100 miles in the next 2 months to get to North Carolina by 2012 is in compensation.  That’s gonna cost $400 in gas, I can handle that, as long as I only drive when it’s below 75 oF so Bessie doesn’t vapour lock.  Yes that’s right, I finally figured out the problem I’ve had since day one, and the remedy I found on the internet?  Tin foil and clothes pins on the fuel line, ideal for Bessie’s style.

The beauty of it down here is me taking one step backwards, two steps forward.  Being able to logically cut through both sides of any political or philosophical issue is utterly useless, I may as well be able to blow smoke rings out my ass.  We’re all flesh, bones and dirt drinking a beer, that’s it, nothing more, nothing less.  The fact I wear a sheriff’s badge on my jacket and jokingly tell people it’s only valid in Canada garners me infinitely more credibility than having a university education.

Um, did anyone know The Beatles named themselves after The Crickets, Buddy Holly’s band?  Yeah, I learned that at the really shitty museum in Lubbock that cost $5, was worth maybe $2 to see the Buddy Holly part, $2.50 to see the seasonal Dia De Los Muertos exhibit (just like the Steinbeck museum in California a year ago, AHHHHH!!).  In short, I want 50 cents back.  The Day of the Dead exhibit did have one real zinger, a painting of Nietzsche all Mexican make-uped that said “Nietzsche is Dead”.  Touche.  Oh, and Elton John started wearing glasses because he wanted to look like Buddy, but they were prescription and he could see properly, so soon enough he’d damaged his vision enough he actually needed glasses.

item.content:encoded:
OK, so it’s actually pronounced “FOOTBALLLLL!!  COOLLLLLLD BEER!!  HAAAAAWWWWT PUSSY!!” then you proceed to down your shot along with the other six people bellied up to the bar yelling the same thing.  I suppose that’s better than when the bartender at a different joint stood on a chair yelling “I might not go down in history, but I’ll go down on your little sister!”

Goddam Democrat ball lickers!!

I realized it was getting time to leave Amarillo after spending another couple nights in the R & R parking lot resulted in me getting offered a job there.  Flattering, sure, but when part of the paycheque was “free beer”, well, I don’t need that.  To my Canadian brain, $1 beers are already “free”, and while I just read that drinking coffee can prevent cirrhosis, I’d rather not make myself any more of a chemical lab rat than I already am.

The road to Lubbock two hours south is flat and easy and I was able to pass towns named Happy and New Deal.  The second I learned used to be called Monroe, but when they applied to get a post office, there was already a Monroe, Texas with a post office so the government decided they’d just call the place New Deal with it being all the rage at the time.  So a town named after Democratic socialism in Texas does actually exists, although in the bathroom at Chili’s in Plainview 40 miles north there was still scribbled on the wall “All Democrats are Maggots”.  I’m still wrestling with whether that’s a misspelling.

Everything IS bigger in Texas, such as these gallon beers

I’ve asked roughly a dozen people what Rick Perry’s deal is, nine told me “he’s been governor since George W became president”, two started immediately going off about how Ron Paul was the only hope the country had and one told me “Rick Perry is a pro-business supply-side conservative who believes trickle-down economics justify cutting school funding to pay for tax breaks for refineries.”  I’m pretty sure the guy who gave me that last statement was gay.  And that’s a compliment down here coming from me, it takes way bigger balls to talk with a lisp and pluck your eyebrows than driving a pickup truck, sporting a dip and a cigarette at the same time while loudly proclaiming Tech can beat the Aggies any day of the week (they didn’t).  I doubt I will see the movie The Sitter, but honestly that line in the trailer is amazing “Can’t buy underwear, balls are too big.”

Speaking of gays and compliments, I quite enjoyed an accidental one I got in R & R one afternoon.  A fellow was telling me about some massive orgy down in New Orleans so I jokingly said I’d have to check it out, to which he immediately responded “oh honey, they’d get one look at you and never let your straight ass through the door.”  Hell yeah!  Balls!

*Blimpy’s anthropological addendum: -Mixed drinks at restaurants as well as bottled liquor at stores weren’t available for sale in Lubbock County until 2009

-Lubbock has the highest religious participation rate in Texas, yet the 6th highest violent crime rate in the entire country.  They also have the highest grossing Chick-Fil-A restaurant in the country because it is a private, religion-centered chicken sandwich restaurant not open on Sunday.

-Iced tea is the second most religiously followed icon behind Christ, green chile sauce and white gravy are tied for third.  White gravy is flour mixed with butter, FYI.

-The #1 convenience store chain in Amarillo is Toot ‘n’ Totem, yet there are none in Lubbock 120 miles south.

-Every bar I went to in Amarillo had a premixed jug of a shot called a Royal Fuck (Crown Royal, Peach Schnapps, cranberry).  No one in Lubbock has ever heard of such a drink.

-I have been informed numerous times to watch out for “Raider Rash”, the local equivalent of gona-herpa-syphillis named after the promiscuous fans of the Texas Tech Raiders.

item.title: Texas Greeting Cards
item.dc:creator: Blimpy
item.description: Wandering the aisles of Target, a birthday card with Obama’s face on it catches my eye… Seen to the right as Exhibit A, as soon as I opened it to hear the accompanying “Spend, spend, spend, spend…” being played out loud, I almost laughed hard enough to drop it. I didn’t realize politics made for [...]
item.content:encoded:
Wandering the aisles of Target, a birthday card with Obama’s face on it catches my eye…

Exhibit A

Seen to the right as Exhibit A, as soon as I opened it to hear the accompanying “Spend, spend, spend, spend…” being played out loud, I almost laughed hard enough to drop it.  I didn’t realize politics made for joke card material, but at least being in a red state they decided to go all out with stereotypical one or two word catch phrases to lambast their President’s “socialist” ways.

Exhibit B

Sure, there were a couple Sarah Palin cards about shooting turkeys or being able to see Russia from your house, but nothing at all knocking her policy or lack thereof.  Searching further I came across Exhibit B which now added Hillary Clinton and Joe Biden to the mix with the outrageous claim that the government being there to “take care of you” was “Dumb, dumb, dumb, dumb…”  I turned to the two Texan friends of mine beside me and semi-angrily barked “do you guys have something against roads and the fire department?!?!”  Considering one of them had just told me at lunch she voted for McCain solely because he was more against abortion than Obama, I believe my latest protest fell on similar deaf ears as my remark at that time “personally I wouldn’t vote for someone to be the leader of the free world if they admitted they didn’t know how to use a computer.”

Exhibit C

Feeling that the best was yet to come, I had to keep digging through the cards to find the holy grail, and Exhibit C was as close as I could come.  Don’t let the Democrats take your candy.  I mean, I know what this means…but what does it mean?!?!  Let’s not even get into the fact you’d only give a card like this to an 8-year-old who would then immediately equate the President with either the boogieman or a schoolyard bully.  I mean, Obama wants to get the people that own the candy factories filled with millions of sweets to just give a handful of them to people working minimum wage buying political Halloween cards at Target…how terrible is that?

Naturally the whole time I couldn’t help thinking of some Canadian equivalent, but we’re short about 25 years of vicious attack ads and Fox News, which these cards are obviously a cultural offshoot of.  Warning, neither of the following two hypothetical lines will make sense to non-Canadians…or be funny to Canadians who get the references.

“Stephen Harper decided to prorogue getting you a gift.”

“Too bad you can’t invoke the notwithstanding clause on getting a year older.”

item.title: Back in the Saddle Again
item.dc:creator: Blimpy
item.description: Me against the world, round 2, ding ding ding. Standing in the dark 10 miles outside Amarillo listening to crickets and semis on the highway, my blood is pumping in a way it hasn’t since May. Every single day you get up is a fight against all things, but we surround ourselves with comfort and [...]
item.content:encoded:
Me against the world, round 2, ding ding ding.

Standing in the dark 10 miles outside Amarillo listening to crickets and semis on the highway, my blood is pumping in a way it hasn’t since May.  Every single day you get up is a fight against all things, but we surround ourselves with comfort and routine as ointment for the battle scars.  The US customs agent before my flight asked what I’d been doing in Calgary during the summer, all I could think to say was “not much”.  People ask me where I’m going next, all I can conjure for a response is “the bar?”

This time around’s going to be a lil’ different.  One, yeah, I haven’t posted in a month, sorry, and I’ll probably be dropping my frequency a bit on this second leg.  Two, as of now the goal is to rip it up for one more year doing the full North America loop, which sorta makes things way easier, it’s just me and Bessie on the war path making hay while the sun shines.

Speaking of the ol’ girl, after sitting in a used car lot for 4 months, it only took about 15 seconds of cranking for the engine to start, the solar panels and stereo still work like a dream, and even though they got three offers on her, my buddies who own the lot were nice enough to not accept any.  Nothing melted, no family of possums, there’s just a bit of a crack in the shit tank, so patch that, get an oil change and I’m off to the races.

Amarillo certainly hasn’t changed while I was gone.  The people who talk the loudest still have the least to say.  When someone drops a reference to their “ex”, they mean ex-wife.  Every single person I asked how the summer was has responded “hot”.

But still, it rocks here.  I’ve already been to R&R three times and the owner, bartenders and regulars all recognize me and ask where my RV’s at.  She’s coming over soon boys, don’t you worry, but in the meantime I need 3 shots of maple syrup and a Rick Perry Is The Future bumper sticker.

A couple Texan buddies down here asked what I thought of the president, so I said he’d been dealt a raw hand but is starting to look like a pussy, then tied in Team America style with the Republicans being dicks and wanting to enslave us all in the robot factories, but none of that mattering because the two parties are just Crest and Colgate, whoever has the most advertizing dollars gets the vote, and the whole system being…..and as I paused to take a breath with my point winding down, I think I got the best response to any spoken word you’ll get around these parts.

“Riiiiiiiiight.”

item.title: The Grass Is Always Greener
item.dc:creator: Blimpy
item.description: Thou shalt not covet has always been funny to me, there’s nothing more human. “I was born and raised in Calgary, but I live in a van in Amarillo Texas.” There was a pause. We glanced at each other sideways. Writing bullshit on a computer screen. Crawling along the edge of a straight razor…and surviving. [...]
item.content:encoded:
Thou shalt not covet has always been funny to me, there’s nothing more human.

“I was born and raised in Calgary, but I live in a van in Amarillo Texas.”  There was a pause.  We glanced at each other sideways.

Writing bullshit on a computer screen.  Crawling along the edge of a straight razor…and surviving.  Time…space…I think I need counselling to stop watching the lady on French Food At Home and singing the theme song to myself when I’m not.

It’s hard to get inspired when you’re not out colliding yourself with the world, but that will recommence in exactly one month.  In the meantime, here’s some macro photos I took in Calgary.

item.title: Deja-vu All Over Again
item.dc:creator: Blimpy
item.description: It’s hard to describe the sheer elation I feel being in the exact same spot in Vancouver I was a year ago. Then I was just coming to grips with my newfound powers, ranting about self-actualization, feeling out the true boundaries of being free as a bird. 4000 miles and 365 days later, I still [...]
item.content:encoded:
It’s hard to describe the sheer elation I feel being in the exact same spot in Vancouver I was a year ago.  Then I was just coming to grips with my newfound powers, ranting about self-actualization, feeling out the true boundaries of being free as a bird.  4000 miles and 365 days later, I still feel somewhat the same, except now more seasoned and in control of exactly how far I can go.  The answer…far.

Vancouver's a hell of a town

Nothing has changed on Broadway Street in Kitsilano save a new dollar store or two opening.  I walk by a Mexican restaurant two blocks away and think to myself that I’d like to try it sometime, then hear echoes of me saying the exact same thing last summer.  Except this time I know how to cook Mexican and would be willing to bet I can do just as good a job.

One of my favourite self-quotes of life advice from the last time I was here was “get rich and piss it all away.”  I obviously haven’t been doing the pissing part properly because I still have enough coin to last for multiple more years when I return to Amarillo in September.  In reality I’ve probably got one more year in me, do the complete loop through the Mississippi river delta, Florida keys and eastern seaboard then be done with it.  I might only make it one if I had to stay in Vancouver and deal with $7 pints and 12% sales tax on everything.  Goddam socialists.

And now there’s a new career path I could start investigating…professionally entering social media intern contests.  I mean in hindsight the Stampede one wasn’t that hard.  Make 1 minute video, vote, win.  Drink, ride horses, tweet about stuff.  Bam, done.  Everyone’s telling me to get the resume updated with that on there, and funnily enough it definitely counts as a job, although I wouldn’t call it working.  And if I felt the need to be sending my resume around Calgary (not gonna happen, don’t worry) I’d get all kinds of bonus street cred if only out of curiousity, whether being a social media intern was applicable to the job or not, at least it proves I’m a real person.

And it’s funny I still feel the need to validate that, perhaps now more than ever.  Blimpy Backgammon, human being.  For all the firebrand vitriol and enlighten thineself this that and the other thing, all I can really ever change is whether I’m sitting or standing, eating or drinking.  And right now I’m going to go sit in the sun and drink a beer.

You want my advice?  Do whatever the fuck you want all the goddam time, that’s all there is to it.

item.title: Calgary Stampede 2011: Staring at the Sun
item.dc:creator: Blimpy
item.description: After leaving my temporary RV home on the Stampede grounds last Monday, it took all the way until Thursday until my brain started remotely working correctly. I was sitting on the front porch in my aviators staring at the sun when I realized all my neurons were firing in the correct order, and it scared [...]
item.content:encoded:
After leaving my temporary RV home on the Stampede grounds last Monday, it took all the way until Thursday until my brain started remotely working correctly.  I was sitting on the front porch in my aviators staring at the sun when I realized all my neurons were firing in the correct order, and it scared me.

About as close as it gets

For those expecting my usual incendiary tone or some sort of expose on how the Stampede really works, I’m afraid that will be hard to provide.  Sure I can dig up a few gripes, but quite honestly that was one of the best weeks of my life, right up there with the one I wrote about when I started my trip a year ago.  That’s sort of the point, quit your day job, sell everything you own and awesome things happen.

Sure, it’s damn near impossible to sleep when the large Stampede crowds don’t disperse until midnight, then although there are 10 times less stragglers wandering out of the bars like Nashville North, they happen to be 10 times drunker and 10 times louder, which is to be expected.  And it doesn’t help when you have events at 6 or 7 AM three days in a row to start the Stampede coupled with about a dozen of your 20 “unique experiences” in the same time frame, but I get it now.

Austin Meier is nails

While I only gained between 250 and 300 Twitter followers and only 88 people have watched my video of riding a chuckwagon (watch it here in HD), the Stampede thought it was a rip roaring success after I did 6 different media spots on Tuesday (good CTV one here).  Apparently Prince Will & Kate provided an estimated 2 to 3 million dollars in free press coverage for the Stampede, so I’m going to run with the assumption they came close to getting their $5000 value in prizes back from me, especially considering they probably only cost the Stampede $2500.  Hell, I already sold the iPhone 4 for twice as much as my “salary”.

But looking back and putting it all in a nutshell, I met Olympic Gold medalists and the second ranked bull rider in North America, rode 65 km/h in a horse-drawn wagon, got to stand on the chuckwagon track during a race and even helped Clint the rodeo clown load up the t-shirt cannon only to watch him shatter a spotlight and spray the crowd with glass.  And this of course glosses over the countless beers and countless pretty ladies.

Incredible colour

If I was going to let fly with one complaint, it was simply being too busy to sit down and enjoy myself and not having the time to create some more of my own content just being myself.  Being told they’re called “product mentions” not “plugs” while getting a list of sponsors to shout out I thought somewhat damaged my credibility as well.  But hey, it’s the first year there’s ever been an Ultimate Stampede Intern, and I sure as hell hope to weasel my way back into future Stampedes in some capacity or another.

Expect a few more post-mortems and me to finally finish editing my Stampede epic pizza time video in the next week or two.  Thanks for following!
